report.text:
EXAM: CT HEAD WITHOUT CONTRAST

ACCESSION: NI9f7fae

CLINICAL HISTORY:
Headache and dizziness.

TECHNIQUE:
Noncontrast axial CT images of the head were obtained with multiplanar reformatted images reviewed.

COMPARISON:
None available.

FINDINGS:

BRAIN:
Small chronic infarct involving the left caudate head and anterior limb of the internal capsule (series 2, image 18).

Mild hyperdense extra-axial collection along the right frontal convexity measuring up to 4 mm in thickness, compatible with a small acute subdural hematoma (series 2, image 27). Mild local sulcal effacement without midline shift.

Rounded hyperdense lesion at the roof of the third ventricle near the foramen of Monro measuring 8 mm, likely colloid cyst (series 2, image 14). No hydrocephalus.

No intraparenchymal hemorrhage. Gray-white differentiation is otherwise preserved.

VENTRICLES/EXTRA-AXIAL SPACES:
No hydrocephalus.

ORBITS:
Unremarkable.

PARANASAL SINUSES/MASTOIDS:
Mild mucosal thickening in the bilateral maxillary sinuses.

BONES:
No acute calvarial fracture.

IMPRESSION:
1. Small acute right frontal convexity subdural hematoma measuring up to 4 mm without significant mass effect or midline shift
2. Probable 8 mm colloid cyst at the roof of the third ventricle near the foramen of Monro without hydrocephalus
3. Chronic infarct involving the left caudate head/anterior limb internal capsule region

findings.patientFriendlyExplanation: There is a small collection of blood on the surface of the brain on the right side, which is causing mild swelling but no significant shift of brain structures.

summary: CT head shows a small acute subdural hematoma on the right, a probable colloid cyst in the third ventricle, and a chronic infarct on the left. No acute fractures or brain tissue bleeding are present.
explanation: You have a small bleed on the surface of your brain (subdural hematoma) and a benign cyst in the center. You also have evidence of an older, healed stroke. These findings may explain your headache and dizziness.
